record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: In a boost-type domain, must every maximal surface be asymptotically flat and coincide with the maximal slices constructed by earlier boost-problem methods?

evidence.quote: Show that a maximal surface in a boost-type domain [COM] is necessarily AF and must coincide with the maximal slices which can be constructed by [BRl; COMB].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth $(n+1)$-dimensional Lorentzian manifold satisfying the vacuum Einstein equations (or, more generally, the dominant energy condition), and let $\Omega \subset M$ be a boost-type domain. Recall that a boost-type domain is, roughly, a region of the form
$$\Omega = \{(t,x) \in \mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R}^n : |t| < \theta(|x|),\; |x| \ge R_0\} \cup \{|x| < R_0\}$$
on which the metric $g$ is asymptotic to the Minkowski metric in the sense that, in suitable coordinates $(t,x^1,\dots,x^n)$, the components $g_{\mu\nu} - \eta_{\mu\nu}$ together with their derivatives decay at appropriate rates as $|x| \to \infty$, uniformly in $t$ for $|t| \le \theta(|x|)$ where $\theta(r) \to \infty$ as $r \to \infty$ (a "boost-type" weighted decay). A spacelike hypersurface $\Sigma \subset \Omega$ is called maximal if its mean curvature vanishes identically.

A spacelike hypersurface $\Sigma$ is called asymptotically flat (AF) if it admits coordinates near infinity in which the induced metric and second fundamental form decay to those of a flat slice of Minkowski spacetime at standard asymptotically flat rates.

Question: Must every maximal spacelike hypersurface $\Sigma \subset \Omega$ in a boost-type domain be asymptotically flat? Moreover, must such $\Sigma$ coincide with a maximal slice obtained from the standard existence constructions for the boost problem (i.e., the maximal hypersurfaces produced by solving the prescribed-mean-curvature-zero equation in boost-type weighted spaces)?
artifact.status_search_result: Existence of maximal hypersurfaces in asymptotically flat and boost-type spacetimes is classical (Bartnik; Christodoulou–Ó Murchadha), and various uniqueness results in asymptotically flat settings have been obtained. However, no specific reference was found establishing that every maximal surface in a general boost-type domain is automatically asymptotically flat and coincides with the slices produced by the standard boost-problem constructions. The status appears unresolved based on available sources.

status_evidence.title: Existence of maximal surfaces in asymptotically flat spacetimes
status_evidence.snippet: Existence theorem for maximal hypersurfaces in asymptotically flat spacetimes (Bartnik).
status_evidence.claim: Existence is established, but the asymptotic-flatness/uniqueness question for maximal surfaces in a boost-type domain is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: On maximal surfaces in asymptotically flat space-times
status_evidence.snippet: Studies of maximal surfaces in asymptotically flat space-times.
status_evidence.claim: Related work, but does not directly settle the boost-type domain rigidity question.

status_evidence.title: Maximal surface - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: General overview of maximal surfaces and existence of maximal hypersurfaces in asymptotically flat Lorentzian manifolds.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms relevance and existence theory but does not state a uniqueness/AF-rigidity result in boost-type domains.
